transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-07-29
Start time: 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE); Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE); Jonah Kim (CSM) ; Dr. Maya Chen (Pioneer Diagnostics); Aaron Li (Pioneer Infra); Sofia Gomez (Pioneer PM)

00:00 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, audio ok? ... cool. We'll keep this to 45, we have the weekly quality eval sync. Agenda is: go over the regression results, prompt tweaks, guardrails, and next steps.
00:18 Dr. Maya Chen: Sounds good. We had a pretty bad run on the last batch, so curious about root cause.
00:25 Lena: Yeah we saw an uptick in hallucinations on the clinical note summarization set - about 12% false assertions vs the baseline 4%. Looks correlated to certain prompt phrasings where the model was asked to 'infer missing context'.
00:40 Aaron: To be clear, this is on the hosted Redwood API? Or on our private pilot infra?
00:47 Samir: These runs were on your Dedicated pilot cluster - the one with the quantized Llama-2 variant you asked to test. So it's not hosted multitenant, it's on your reserved nodes.
01:02 Sofia: Got it. So what's the leading hypothesis? Prompt framing or model variant?
01:09 Lena: Hypothesis is twofold: prompt framing + cached prefix behaviors. We noticed some KV cache reuse across similar patient note prefixes - which gave some stale context. Also the quantization stepping caused small tokenization oddities for rare tokens (we saw weird token splitting around lab values.)
01:33 Dr. Maya Chen: Token splitting - can that create hallucinations? I thought that's more a fidelity / numeric precision problem.
01:40 Lena: It can. If numeric tokens get split differently, the model's attention patterns shift and it might fabricate values to reconcile. Also the prompt that asked to 'assume' missing values gave it license to invent. So prompt guardrails need to be stricter: explicit "do not assume facts, if missing say 'unknown'".
02:07 Jonah: Quick note - transcription's messy on some proper nouns, apologies.
02:11 Aaron: Also we saw a latency bump when we increased batch size to reduce CPU cycles. Was there a tradeoff there?
02:19 Lena: Yes. Larger batching reduces tokens/sec cost but increases p50 latency a bit. On your SLA target 200ms p50 for short summarization calls, we were hitting 260ms with batch size 8. We can tune the batching policy or use a warm pool to improve p50.
02:36 Dr. Maya Chen: Warm pool meaning keep GPUs warm with prefix caching?
02:41 Lena: Prefix/KV cache warm pools - yes. For small low-latency calls we recommend aggressive caching of common templates, and a smaller dedicated fast path for p50 sensitive routes.
02:53 Sofia: Are there any model-level fixes - e.g., move to a non-quantized float16 variant?
02:58 Samir: That's an option - float16 improves numeric fidelity but cost goes up ~2.2x. There's also a middle ground: 8-bit quant with per-channel calibration, which reduces cost but improves token splitting artifacts.
03:16 Aaron: Do you have numbers on token cost delta? Our procurement team is watching budget.
03:22 Samir: For your Pilot usage we estimate hosted token cost equivalent at ~ $0.0008/token for float16 and ~ $0.00035/token for 8-bit quant, ballpark. We'll send a more detailed projection.
03:36 Dr. Maya Chen: Back to the regression: Did you run our regression suite against the new prompt set we shipped last week?
03:43 Lena: Yes. We ran the suite - baseline precision dropped on three categories: lab-value extraction, medication timeliness, and assertion hallucinations. We flagged 42 failing prompts out of 350. Many were in the family of 'summarize and infer' templates.
04:05 Sofia: Is there a way to automatically detect 'assume' language in prompts in order to block them or rewrite them?
04:12 Lena: We can add a lightweight prompt linter - match for words like 'assume' 'infer' 'guess' and rewrite to 'if unknown, respond "unknown"'. Also we can apply a safety filter post-hoc that checks generated facts against the source text and penalizes unsupported assertions.
04:30 Aaron: For the safety filter, does that run on the same cluster? Extra compute?
04:35 Lena: It can be implemented as a lightweight comparator on the inference path - a small retriever + fuzzy match. It's additional compute but relatively low compared to the generation pass. We can also run it asynchronously for non-blocking flows.
04:52 Samir: On the topic of guardrails, we also recommend a two-step: local prompt-level guardrail + output classifier that flags potential hallucinations. If flagged, either return 'uncertain' or trigger a higher-quality generation from float16.
05:08 Dr. Maya Chen: Ok interesting. What's the false positive rate on the classifier?
05:12 Lena: Right now our eval shows 8% false positive at 95% recall on hallucinations. Tuning can reduce that but increases recall vs precision tradeoff.
05:25 Jonah: We also noted some mismatches in scoring thresholds - QA score vs human label alignment. That may be why some failure counts look worse than expected.
05:33 Lena: Good point. Our automated BLEU/ROUGE-like scorers don't capture clinical correctness well. We're switching to task-specific metrics for lab extraction and assertion detection; F1 on entity spans and a custom entailment check for assertions.
05:49 Sofia: For the customer side, we can provide more annotated examples to improve the entailment model.
05:54 Dr. Maya Chen: We'll add edge cases especially negations and temporal phrases - 'no longer on X since last visit' - those trip things up.
06:03 Aaron: Security quick Q - if we move to Private deployment in our VPC, how will KMS work? We need HSM integration for PHI.
06:12 Samir: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM connectors. We integrate with AWS KMS and partner HSM; logs are exported to your SIEM. We'll share SOC2 + integration docs.
06:24 Aaron: Great. Any compliance impact if we switch quantization codecs? No, right?
06:29 Lena: No. Quantization is a local model-optimization step; it doesn't change data residency or encryption at rest policies. We'll document the build process for audit.
06:40 Dr. Maya Chen: Regarding regression root cause: can you run an ablation that toggles only the prompt rewrite vs only the non-quantized model so we can see which fixes most of the failing prompts?
06:51 Lena: Yes we can run three ablations: (A) prompt rewrites + guardrail enabled; (B) switch to float16 variant; (C) both. We'll produce a small matrix of pass/fail counts per category.
07:05 Samir: Timeline - we can deliver the ablation results in 6 business days if you give the additional 200 validation prompts we requested.
07:12 Dr. Maya Chen: We can deliver those by Tuesday. Also can you include the raw generation examples so our clinicians can review?
07:19 Lena: We'll include the raw generations and an anonymized trace that shows the prefix/KV cache state and model variant used.
07:28 Aaron: Network: we need to confirm egress policies. If private deployment, will Redwood require specific outbound endpoints for model updates?
07:36 Samir: For Private we do periodic model artifact pulls; those can be pinned and you can opt for air-gapped update windows. We'll get the documentation.
07:45 Jonah: Quick FYI - we logged this call in the CRM under deal PD-2026-07; adding notes.
07:51 Dr. Maya Chen: Any blockers from Redwood side that we should know?
07:55 Samir: Nothing blocking - just need the prompts and confirm if you want ablation C prioritized. Also confirm if the procurement team wants the float16 cost estimate for budgeting.
08:08 Sofia: We'll ask procurement but lean toward trying prompt guardrails first before increasing spend.
08:16 Samir: Great. Recap of next steps...

08:20 Recap & Next Steps
08:21 Samir: 1) Samir to share updated pricing and pilot usage estimate by 2026-08-02.
08:29 Samir: 2) Lena to run ablations (prompt rewrite / float16 / both) and send results with raw generations by 2026-08-05.
08:37 Dr. Maya Chen: 3) Pioneer to provide 200 additional validation prompts and sensitive PII list by 2026-08-04.
08:44 Aaron: 4) Schedule infra deep-dive on private deployment week of 2026-08-10 - I'll coordinate with Samir.
08:51 Samir: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the thread. Chat me if anything urgent.
09:00 Meeting ends

Notes: Shared artifacts: 'pioneer_pilot_regression_summary.pdf' (link in email), 'ablation-plan.xlsx', 'redwood-security-soc2-kms.pdf'

Transcript quality: medium - some noise and mis-attributed speaker lines, timestamps approximate.
